input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer at 15% of annual Fees for every week an invoice is late, triggered by a mere ten-day payment delay. That fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees), and it sits in walk-away territory because the compounding weekly charge can quickly exceed the remaining contract value and is triggered by a minor breach. No other provision imposes Customer-payable liquidated damages, minimum fees, or shortfall charges (Sections 9.4 and 10 confirm Customer owes only accrued Fees on termination). Redline deletes the liquidated damages and substitutes customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, preserving the Section 7.3 withholding right.

proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, and 15% of annual Fees per week of delay is punitive and could exceed the contract value. We have replaced it with customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with the dispute-withholding right in Section 7.3.

ops.newText: 7.7 If a proper, undisputed invoice remains unpaid thirty days after its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at one percent per month (or the highest rate permitted by Applicable Law, if lower) from the due date until payment. No liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer under this Agreement.
